# Pandamonium v1.0.67

This train makes arbitrary repository pastes behave: the scanner classifies by what a repository actually is (so a Go movie CLI is no longer reported as a skill package), installed GitHub plugins now appear in the Marketplace with honest provenance, and an installed plugin can be offered into the marketplace as a reviewable submission bundle. The composer reasoning spec also got a loaded-runner timeout so the browser gate stops flaking.

## MAD-955 — Scan: classify by primary purpose (Go/Rust/toolchains) and never draft skills from incidental skill folders

### Problem

Pasting `https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/pandaflix` (a Go movie CLI) classified the whole repository as `skill_bundle` and drafted a "Pandaflix" skill extension, because the repository carries `.opencode/skills/caveman/SKILL.md` for its own dev tooling. `_classify` returned `skill_bundle` when any `*SKILL.md` existed anywhere before checking `go.mod`/`pyproject.toml`/`package.json`/MCP/OpenAPI/web signals, and Go and Rust repositories had no recognition at all. The single-candidate skill fallback then drafted from any incidental skill folder.

### Implementation

Classification now runs by primary purpose: committed `jarvis-extension.json` first, then an explicit `.codex-plugin`/`.claude-plugin` descriptor that declares skills, then toolchain signals (Go, Rust, MCP, Python, Node, OpenAPI, web, container service), and skills only when a root `SKILL.md` exists or canonical `skills/` content is the repository's primary surface. New repo classes `go_cli`, `go_module`, `rust_cli`, `rust_lib`, and `service` are added to scan validation and the schema, and `go.mod`/`Cargo.toml` dependencies are parsed into the scan result. The single-directory skill fallback now only considers canonical `skills/` content. Unsupported classes produce no draft and the intake UI names the class honestly ("This looks like a Go command-line tool… Nothing was ingested"). Scan progress gained an elapsed-time ticker and a working shimmer so a long fetch never looks dead. Feature commit `8b69a25f`, PR #254.

### Product value and UI visibility

The operator can paste any public repository and get a truthful classification, dependencies, licenses, and findings without accidentally drafting a skill package from a repository's internal dev tooling. Go and Rust projects get real dependency inventories even though Pandamonium does not install them as plugins yet.

### Verification

Red-first precedence tests: pandaflix-shaped Go CLI → `go_cli`, no draft, no skill capabilities, Go dependency parsed; Rust CLI vs library split; declared skill plugin beats `package.json`; root `SKILL.md` → `skill_bundle`; container-only repository → `service`. Real-repo check: pandaflix drafts nothing as `go_cli` with 27 Go dependencies and GPL-3.0/BSD-3-Clause licenses. Full Python suite 6403 passed / 5 skipped; intake browser specs 5/5; full Chromium 180 passed at merge.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency or schema-breaking change; the scan artifact gains new `repo_class` enum values and existing artifacts remain valid. Go/Rust scans are informational only: no binary is built, executed, or installed. A repository that genuinely ships skills from non-canonical directories without a descriptor is now reported as `unknown` rather than drafted.

### References

## MAD-954 — Marketplace: show installed plugins from every origin with provenance detail

### Problem

Installed plugins from GitHub intake never appeared in the Marketplace tab — only the signed catalog entry (ORACLE) showed — because Marketplace rendered only `/api/extensions/marketplace`. The operator asked why the plugins they install are not in the marketplace.

### Implementation

The Marketplace now merges the signed catalog with every installed registry extension, deduplicated by id. GitHub-intake rows carry a `GitHub intake` badge, a revision-based provenance block, not-catalog-signed signature/review copy, and installed-state lifecycle actions (Disable/Enable/Remove) through the existing lifecycle preview; configured surfaces show `Configured` with no lifecycle actions; catalog entries keep `Verified`/`Signed` badges and their full detail. Offline, empty, and verification-failed catalog states keep their explicit notice and still list installed plugins. Feature commit `8f017bdf`, PR #256.

### Product value and UI visibility

One Marketplace surface now tells the truth about everything installed: what came from the signed catalog and what was installed from GitHub intake, with the pinned revision visible and lifecycle actions reachable from the same detail panel.

### Verification

New browser spec covers the intake-installed row appearing in Marketplace with the source badge, no `Verified` claim, `Not catalog-signed` provenance, and Disable/Remove actions; offline and empty states keep their notices while installed rows stay visible. Full Chromium suite 182 passed; marketplace specs 9/9.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No API or schema change; the merge is a client-side projection of existing endpoints. Source URLs inside installed extension records deliberately remain unexposed by the installed view (privacy), so intake provenance shows origin plus pinned revision rather than the raw repository URL.

### References

## MAD-956 — Marketplace: offer an installed GitHub plugin as a reviewable submission artifact

### Problem

An installed GitHub-intake plugin was a dead end: "we're the devs, so if we make it work for us we offer it into the marketplace", but there was no path from an installed plugin into the signed catalog.

### Implementation

New admin route `POST /api/extensions/installed/{id}/submissions` builds a deterministic, unsigned submission bundle: manifest, pinned revision, capability inventory, permissions, data boundaries, and configuration declarations (key names, never values). Bundles are written under `<EXTENSIONS_DIR>/submissions/<id>/<revision>/submission.json` with a canonical `sha256` digest, and duplicate offers for the same revision are idempotent. The Marketplace detail for intake plugins gains **Offer to marketplace…** and shows submission state, digest, bundle path, and an explicit "publishing stays offline with the release tooling" note. Missing, disabled, or non-registry extensions fail closed; the app never reads or stores a signing key. Feature commit `3336d300`, PR #259.

### Product value and UI visibility

The dev workflow the operator asked for: install from GitHub, verify it works, then offer that exact pinned revision for marketplace review with one click and a verifiable digest — without any runtime signing authority in the web app.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_submission.py` covers digest determinism, idempotent duplicate offers, declarations-not-values, and missing/disabled guards; the route-contract test pins the admin gate; the browser spec drives the offer action and asserts the displayed digest and offline-publishing note. Full Python suite 6406 passed / 5 skipped; marketplace browser specs 9/9.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Submissions are review artifacts only — no automatic publication and no catalog writes. Curators still publish through the existing offline catalog tooling with the release keys. Submission history keeps one bundle per revision; a later revision produces a new bundle.

### References

- [Linear MAD-956](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-956)
- [GitHub issue #258](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/issues/258)

## MAD-952 — Composer reasoning controls (test-hardening provenance)

### Problem

The composer reasoning spec failed twice on loaded CI runners while validating the v1.0.66/v1.0.67 work: `#composer-effort-value` still read `Default` after the 5s default timeout (14 polls), blocking otherwise-green pull requests.

### Implementation

The feature shipped in v1.0.65; this train only carries a test-only hardening commit (`62791ab7`, PR #257) that gives the two effort-value assertions a 20s window so a late-settling label on slow runners no longer fails the browser gate.

### Product value and UI visibility

No user-facing change. The composer control itself is unchanged from v1.0.65; CI stops rerunning the same unrelated job.

### Verification

The hardened spec passes on the loaded CI runner (PR #257 green) and locally; no application behavior changed.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Test-only timeout change; no runtime, dependency, or schema impact.

### References

- [Linear MAD-952](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-952)
- [Reasoning spec timeout PR #257](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/257)
